title: Skills I Use: choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Line Timetable. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Line Timetable
options.lineage: printed transit timetables and network diagrams
options.thesis: Five skills set as five lines on one network: each has a route colour, a numbered stop list, and a place on the map.
options.viewport: Left: a contents rail drawn as a line diagram with five coloured stops. Centre: title, two-sentence intro, then the quick-install block set as a ruled timetable, one row per command with a copy control. Each skill section opens with a route band, line number and pitch.
options.risk: Five route colours can turn loud; they must stay as thin bands and markers, never fills behind text.

raised.raise: Everything registers against one off-centre rail: the route line runs the full page and every section, command and note hangs off it.
Sections descend in the order work happens: write code, shape UI, check what ships.

options.label: The Printed Manual
options.lineage: white-cover programming manuals and their numbered sections
options.thesis: A short technical manual: numbered chapters, a serif reading column, large mono listings, a running head.
options.viewport: Left: numbered contents. Centre: chapter-style title, intro in a serif column, then listing 0.1, the quick-install commands, in a ruled code block with copy controls. Skill sections are chapters 1 to 5 with margin labels for Install, Benefits, Example.
options.risk: Also where most documentation pages in this category land; it reads correct more than distinct.

options.label: Swiss Grid Series
options.thesis: One strict module, five posters: each skill gets a geometric mark and a large numeral, all on the same grid.
options.viewport: A 12-column grid shown plainly. Title set large flush left across eight columns, contents as a typographic list in the last four, quick-install below as rows on the module. Each skill opens with a numeral and its own bar-and-arc figure.
options.case: Holds product clarity: the grid makes commands and benefits easy to scan. Loses on audience identification: developers read it as a design exercise first.
options.risk: Large numerals and geometry push the commands further down the page.

options.label: Emission-Line Rail
options.thesis: Everything hangs off one calibrated rail on a charcoal continuum.
options.viewport: A rail with five ticks; the open one blooms into a plate.
options.case: Single type size and dark-only ground fight a light and dark reference page that prints on A4.
options.risk: Navigation the reader has to learn.
options.kept: One rail that every element registers against.

options.label: Stitched Sampler
options.thesis: Bands stacked in order of difficulty, signed at the foot.
options.viewport: Stacked bands, one per skill, loosening down the sheet.
options.case: Senior developers do not see themselves in it, and stitched type hurts command legibility.
options.kept: Bands ordered as the work actually progresses.

options.label: Cutting Bench
options.thesis: A perforated rail of frames across a grain-orange field.
options.viewport: Frames strung on a rail, prose in white windows.
options.case: Orange on a third of the screen and a scrubbing strip work against calm reading and print.
options.kept: State shown as a mark, not a hue.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: One long building section with a sunbeam as the active band.
options.viewport: A continuous section with annotations pinned to sun angles.
options.case: No true mapping from skills to rooms and light; the metaphor would have to be invented.
options.kept: Annotations pinned to the thing they describe.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: A flat black plane that one gold cord pulls into volume.
options.viewport: A semicircle that gathers as sections open.
options.case: Fashion grammar says nothing to this audience and adds a transformation the content does not need.
options.kept: One accent that is also the control.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A standard docs site: sidebar, content column, on-this-page list.
canonCard.viewport: Top bar, left sidebar, centred content with a quick-install code block, right-hand section list.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other docs page by design.
